sentences.latin: Puella aviam bonam habet.
sentences.english: The girl has a good grandmother.

sentences.latin: Avia a puella amatur.
sentences.english: The grandmother is loved by the girl.

sentences.latin: Avia donum pulchrum parat.
sentences.english: The grandmother prepares a beautiful gift.

sentences.latin: Puella donum novum aperit.
sentences.english: The girl opens the new gift.

sentences.latin: Puella in dono librum magnum videt.
sentences.english: The girl sees a large book in the gift.

sentences.latin: Avia puellam ad flumen ducit.
sentences.english: The grandmother leads the girl to the river.

sentences.latin: Sed puella librum portat.
sentences.english: But the girl carries the book.

sentences.latin: Avia et puella pisces parvos vident.
sentences.english: The grandmother and the girl see the small fish.

sentences.latin: Flores albi ab avia portantur.
sentences.english: The white flowers are carried by the grandmother.

sentences.latin: Itaque puella aviam et flumen amat.
sentences.english: And so the girl loves the grandmother and the river.

sentences.latin: Iudex iustus in civitate nostra leges custodit.
sentences.english: The just judge guards the laws in our state.

sentences.latin: Femina misera verba sua iudici dicit.
sentences.english: The wretched woman speaks her own words to the judge.

sentences.latin: Iudex verba feminae audit et veritatem quaerit.
sentences.english: The judge hears the woman's words and seeks the truth.

sentences.latin: Sed vir ferox contra feminam verba multa dicit.
sentences.english: But a fierce man speaks many words against the woman.

sentences.latin: Nam vir ferox feminae miserae invidet.
sentences.english: For the fierce man envies the wretched woman.

sentences.latin: Sed iudex sapiens feminae miserae credit.
sentences.english: But the wise judge believes the wretched woman.

sentences.latin: Itaque femina misera a iudice iusto servatur.
sentences.english: And so the wretched woman is protected by the just judge.

sentences.latin: Populus civitatis virum ferocem videt et verba iudicis audit.
sentences.english: The people of the state see the fierce man and hear the judge's words.

sentences.latin: Nam lex nostra a populo fideli amatur.
sentences.english: For our law is loved by the loyal people.

sentences.latin: Itaque veritas et libertas in civitate nostra servantur.
sentences.english: And so truth and freedom are preserved in our state.

sentences.latin: Agricolae miseri oppidi nostri a dracone feroci montis alti terrentur.
sentences.english: The wretched farmers of our town are frightened by the fierce dragon of the high mountain.
